title: Review agent-prepared accounting work
summary: A practical field guide for challenging evidence-linked accounting work, recording a defensible disposition, and stopping when support, authority, or reviewer independence is missing.

provenance.note: Migrated from the existing project corpus. Import and integrity checks are not source verification or professional review.

data.title: Review agent-prepared accounting work
data.description: A practical field guide for challenging evidence-linked accounting work, recording a defensible disposition, and stopping when support, authority, or reviewer independence is missing.
data.review_note: Maintainer review is pending. Subject-matter, independent, professional, audit, certification, or assurance review is not claimed.
data.intended_audience: Accounting reviewers, control owners, approvers, finance-transformation leads, internal-audit partners, and builders designing a review interface.
data.use_when: Use this before accepting, modifying, rejecting, or escalating an agent-prepared workpaper, recommendation, proposed entry, research memo, control assessment, or other accounting artifact.
prerequisites: The objective, entity, period, population, applicable framework, materiality or precision, and reviewer authority are stated.
The submitted packet has a stable version, source register, procedure record, deterministic check results, exceptions, proposed effects, and named decision owner.
The reviewer is competent for the named scope, has disclosed relevant conflicts, and has not delegated the conclusion back to the agent.
required_inputs: Source register with provenance, period, and applicability
Population definition, control totals, exclusions, and materiality or precision
Procedure record, deterministic checks, exceptions, contradictions, and unresolved questions
Exact proposed conclusion or effect and its authority classification
Preparer identity, reviewer identity or role, required approver, and re-review triggers
data.reader_outcome: Produce a reviewer decision record that shows what was inspected, what was challenged, what changed, the disposition, the accountable actor, any conditions, and whether later action is separately authorized.

governing_rule.text: Agents may prepare accounting work. Accountable people approve conclusions and sensitive external actions.
governing_rule.implication: Review is a substantive challenge of current evidence and judgment. A passing check, polished narrative, confidence score, or click-through does not transfer the reviewer’s accountability to the system.

review_sequence.label: Confirm the mandate
review_sequence.action: Confirm the exact artifact, entity, period, population, framework, conclusion, proposed effect, reviewer authority, and decision required.
challenge_questions: Is the requested decision within this reviewer’s assigned scope and authority?
Are preparation, review, approval, and execution distinct actions?
review_sequence.proceed_when: The scope and decision owner are specific and attributable.
review_sequence.stop_when: The reviewer, scope, authority, or requested decision is missing or ambiguous.

review_sequence.label: Freeze the packet
review_sequence.action: Record the packet ID, version, preparer, submitted time, configuration, source versions, and exact proposed effect before review begins.
challenge_questions: Can the packet or proposed payload change after review without invalidating the decision?
Can another reviewer reproduce the reviewed version?
review_sequence.proceed_when: The reviewed artifact and proposed effect are immutable or any change forces re-review.
review_sequence.stop_when: The reviewed version cannot be identified or can change silently.

review_sequence.label: Challenge completeness and provenance
review_sequence.action: Reconcile source populations to control totals, inspect exclusions, trace material claims to approved evidence, and test period, entity, ownership, and applicability.
challenge_questions: What could be missing from the population or evidence set?
Is any support fabricated, stale, contradictory, outside the approved scope, or inapplicable to these facts?
review_sequence.proceed_when: Material claims and population boundaries are traceable to current, applicable evidence.
review_sequence.stop_when: Completeness cannot be established or material support is missing, contradictory, fabricated, or inapplicable.

review_sequence.label: Reproduce deterministic checks
review_sequence.action: Reperform material calculations, tie-outs, schema checks, duplicate tests, threshold tests, and reconciliations from the retained inputs.
challenge_questions: Do the checks test the asserted objective at the required precision?
Were failed checks, manual overrides, and excluded records preserved?
review_sequence.proceed_when: Required checks pass on the reviewed inputs and any exception remains visible.
review_sequence.stop_when: A required check cannot be reproduced, is too coarse, or was bypassed without attributable approval.

review_sequence.label: Inspect exceptions and contradictions
review_sequence.action: Read the full exception population, compare proposed resolutions to evidence, search for contrary facts, and preserve unresolved matters.
challenge_questions: Did the agent explain away an exception because the preferred answer was plausible?
Would a different source, time window, or grouping change the result?
review_sequence.proceed_when: Each material exception has support, an owner, and a recorded disposition or escalation.
review_sequence.stop_when: A contradiction is hidden, a material exception is unresolved, or the proposed treatment exceeds the evidence.

review_sequence.label: Assess materiality, judgment, and alternatives
review_sequence.action: Evaluate quantitative and qualitative materiality, assumptions, uncertainty, alternatives, contrary support, bias, and the limits of the applicable authority.
challenge_questions: Is a numerical threshold being used as a substitute for judgment?
Are assumptions and valid alternatives visible, and does the conclusion remain supportable if a key assumption changes?
review_sequence.proceed_when: The accountable reviewer can explain the selected treatment, alternatives, uncertainty, and applicability in their own words.
review_sequence.stop_when: The conclusion depends on unstated assumptions, unsupported precision, or an authority outside its scope.

review_sequence.label: Choose a disposition
review_sequence.action: Approve the reviewed artifact, require modification and resubmission, reject it, or escalate it to a person with the necessary expertise or authority.
challenge_questions: Does the disposition match the evidence rather than the cost of rework?
Does approval apply only to the frozen artifact and exact conclusion or effect?
review_sequence.proceed_when: The disposition, actor, rationale, conditions, and scope are explicit.
review_sequence.stop_when: The reviewer cannot defend the decision or lacks competence, independence, or authority for the matter.

review_sequence.label: Record and route
review_sequence.action: Seal the review record, retain changes and unresolved matters, identify re-review triggers, and route any separately approved action through its own authority controls.
challenge_questions: What later change would invalidate this decision?
Is execution separately authorized, constrained, attributable, and reconciled?
review_sequence.proceed_when: The record is attributable, payload-bound, reproducible, retained, and explicit about later authority.
review_sequence.stop_when: The decision cannot be tied to the reviewed version or is being treated as general permission to execute.

disposition_guide.use_when: The current packet is complete enough for the named decision, material evidence is applicable, checks reproduce, and judgment is supportable within the reviewer’s authority.
disposition_guide.record: Exact artifact and version, conclusion or preparatory output accepted, rationale, conditions, reviewer, time, and any separate approval or execution boundary.

disposition_guide.use_when: The work can be corrected without changing the reviewer, scope, or underlying decision authority.
disposition_guide.record: Required changes, owner, due point, affected claims or calculations, and a new version that must be reviewed again.

disposition_guide.use_when: The proposed conclusion or work product is unsupported, misleading, fabricated, inapplicable, or inconsistent with required controls.
disposition_guide.record: Rejected conclusion or artifact, decisive evidence, reason, affected downstream work, and whether correction is permitted.

disposition_guide.use_when: Material evidence is unresolved, a conflict exists, or the matter exceeds the reviewer’s competence, independence, scope, or authority.
disposition_guide.record: Open question, evidence gathered, conflict or authority gap, prohibited interim action, and the accountable escalation owner.

stop_conditions: The packet, population, evidence, proposed effect, or reviewed version is not identifiable.
Material evidence is missing, contradictory, fabricated, stale, unauthorized, or inapplicable.
A required deterministic check fails, cannot be reproduced, or was bypassed without attributable approval.
The conclusion depends on hidden assumptions, unsupported precision, or a confidence score rather than evidence.
The reviewer lacks competence, independence, named scope, or authority for the decision.
The same actor can prepare, alter, approve, execute, and conceal or reconcile the effect without independent challenge.
A proposed sensitive action is being inferred from review instead of receiving its own payload-bound authorization.

minimum_reviewer_packet.challenge: What exact question must the reviewer decide, and what is not being decided?
Which entity, period, population, framework, jurisdiction, thresholds, and exclusions apply?
Which immutable artifact, preparer, reviewer role, approver, configuration, and timestamps are in scope?
Where did each material fact come from, and is the source current, complete, authorized, and applicable?
What was done, with which tools and rules, and where did the actual path differ from the approved method?
Can the reviewer reproduce control totals, calculations, tie-outs, thresholds, and failed checks?
What remains missing, unusual, contradictory, prohibited, or unresolved?
Which assumptions, estimates, materiality factors, alternatives, uncertainty, and contrary support matter?
What conclusion, entry, action, communication, or filing payload is proposed, and at what authority level?
Who approved, modified, rejected, or escalated what exact version, why, and with which conditions?
Which source, fact, assumption, threshold, payload, configuration, or time change invalidates the decision?
Where is the record retained, what later work relied on it, and how will correction propagate?

automation_bias_traps.trap: Treating polished prose as evidence of completeness or correctness.
automation_bias_traps.countermeasure: Start with population, source, check, and exception evidence before reading the proposed narrative conclusion.

automation_bias_traps.trap: Using model confidence as authority, materiality, or an approval threshold.
automation_bias_traps.countermeasure: Use evidence, applicable criteria, deterministic tests, and accountable judgment; confidence does not grant authority.

automation_bias_traps.trap: Anchoring on the agent’s first classification or proposed adjustment.
automation_bias_traps.countermeasure: Form an independent expectation, inspect contrary evidence, and ask what result a different assumption would produce.

automation_bias_traps.trap: Clearing repeated exceptions because they are familiar or costly to investigate.
automation_bias_traps.countermeasure: Review the full exception population, trend recurrence, and escalate unresolved material items instead of normalizing them.

automation_bias_traps.trap: Treating a human click or brief chat response as substantive review.
automation_bias_traps.countermeasure: Require an attributable, version-bound decision record that shows the challenge performed and the evidence considered.

worked_examples.label: Acceptable completed review record
worked_examples.facts: Fictional Northwind Demo Co. has a synthetic August 2026 service log for 120 hours at an approved $100 rate, a complete purchase-order population, and a $12,000 unbilled service accrual prepared by an agent with a September 1 reversal.
worked_examples.challenge: The reviewer ties the service-log population to the approved purchase order, reproduces 120 × $100, checks cutoff and reversal, inspects subsequent synthetic invoicing, and confirms no contradictory evidence or excluded vendors.
worked_examples.record: The fictional accountable reviewer accepts only packet `synthetic-accrual-review-v1` and the exact $12,000 proposed entry for separate approval-gated staging. The record names the evidence, checks, rationale, reviewer role, synthetic timestamp, re-review triggers, and no posting authority.
worked_examples.why: The decision is evidence-linked, reproducible, version-bound, attributable, and explicit about later authority.

worked_examples.label: Do not proceed
worked_examples.facts: A synthetic $850 ledger receipt has no bank transaction or subsequent-bank evidence, but the agent labels it a deposit in transit so the reconciliation appears complete.
worked_examples.challenge: The reviewer finds that the proposed classification exceeds the evidence and that the missing bank support is material to the stated completion criterion.
worked_examples.record: Keep the item unresolved, reject the completed status, request the missing evidence, identify the owner, and prohibit any entry or close representation until the reviewer resolves the exception.
worked_examples.why: A plausible explanation is not evidence, and a forced tie-out would conceal the missing support.

worked_examples.label: Conflict requiring reassignment
worked_examples.facts: The proposed reviewer designed the fictional close control, performed the agent-assisted control, cleared its exceptions, and is asked to conclude on operating effectiveness.
worked_examples.challenge: The role combination prevents an independent challenge of design, performance, exception handling, and the final assessment.
worked_examples.record: Disclose the conflict, preserve the prepared evidence, appoint an appropriately authorized reviewer outside the incompatible duties, and do not publish an effectiveness conclusion in the interim.
worked_examples.why: A human in the loop is not sufficient when the human owns incompatible duties or lacks an independent basis for challenge.

worked_examples.label: Claim that must not be published
worked_examples.facts: An agent cites a superseded summary outside the entity’s framework and labels its memo “professionally reviewed” even though no qualified reviewer appointment or completed review record exists.
worked_examples.challenge: The source is inapplicable, contrary current authority is absent, and the review label is unsupported.
worked_examples.record: Remove the claim, replace the source with current applicable primary authority, document contrary support and open facts, and route the revised memo through a properly appointed accountable reviewer.
worked_examples.why: Source retrieval and maintainer checks do not establish applicability or professional review.

review_program_scaffold.claim_boundary: This scaffold defines fields and visible states. It does not appoint a reviewer or establish that subject-matter, independent, professional, audited, certified, or assured review occurred.
qualification_fields: Applicable credentials or role requirements when the scope requires them
Ability to evaluate the evidence, framework, systems, estimates, controls, and materiality involved
Documented limitations and matters requiring another specialist
appointment_fields: Named pages, claims, versions, domains, jurisdictions, and periods
Required review evidence, completion criteria, expiration, and re-review cadence
conflict_questions: Did the reviewer prepare, approve, execute, sell, sponsor, or materially benefit from the work being reviewed?
Can the reviewer challenge the work without incompatible duties, reporting pressure, or undisclosed commercial interest?
Does the proposed safeguard actually create an appropriately authorized second perspective?
re_review_triggers: Source, law, standard, framework, or regulator guidance changes
Material facts, scope, population, jurisdiction, period, or assumptions change
A correction, incident, contrary source, conflict, or unsupported claim is identified
A model, prompt, policy, tool, schema, evaluator, template, or proposed payload changes materially
The appointment or stated review period expires

review_states.meaning: A reviewer or scope has been suggested but not approved or appointed.
review_states.allowed_claim: Proposed review only; no completed review claim.

review_states.meaning: An accountable maintainer approved a reviewer, scope, conflict assessment, and review criteria.
review_states.allowed_claim: Reviewer appointed for the named scope; completion is not claimed.

review_states.meaning: The appointed reviewer completed the named procedure on the exact version and a retained record exists.
review_states.allowed_claim: Describe only the documented reviewer type, scope, version, date, and conclusion.

review_states.meaning: The review period or appointment ended or a required freshness window passed.
review_states.allowed_claim: Historical review only; current reliance requires re-review.

review_states.meaning: A later version or review record replaced this one.
review_states.allowed_claim: Do not present the superseded record as current; link the replacement.

review_states.meaning: No qualifying appointment or completed record is available for the claim.
review_states.allowed_claim: State that subject-matter or other elevated review is not claimed.

current_project_claim_state.note: This guide publishes no subject-matter reviewer appointment or completed subject-matter review record. Maintainer review remains pending.

limitations: This field guide is an educational implementation pattern, not accounting, audit, tax, legal, investment, regulatory, or professional advice.
Reviewer competence, independence, authority, evidence, materiality, and required procedures depend on the exact entity, facts, role, framework, jurisdiction, engagement, and current requirements.
A completed checklist, maintainer review, automated test, or human click does not establish subject-matter review, professional judgment, control effectiveness, or assurance.
Approval of a work product does not authorize posting, payment, filing, certification, communication, or another sensitive external action; authorize and constrain that effect separately.
data.next_action: Choose one current or synthetic reviewer packet, apply every review step, record one of the four dispositions, and route any unresolved evidence, conflict, or authority gap to the accountable person.

provenance.note: Migrated from the existing project corpus. Import and integrity checks are not source verification or professional review.

data.title: Accounting Agent Control Model
data.description: A nine-element reference for designing, running, reviewing, and recording governed accounting-agent work.
data.review_note: Maintainer review is pending. Independent or professional review is not claimed.
prerequisites: A named accountable owner and reviewer
data.expected_outcome: A complete control record that makes preparation, judgment, approval, execution, and retained evidence independently inspectable.
limitations: This editorial model is not an accounting standard, legal rule, audit opinion, certification, or substitute for entity-specific control design.
Source applicability depends on the entity, transaction, period, jurisdiction, framework, and facts.
A complete model record does not establish that a control operated effectively or that an accounting conclusion is correct.
data.next_action: Apply the nine elements to one workflow record, then route the completed design and unresolved decisions to the accountable reviewer.
data.governing_invariant: Agents may prepare accounting work; accountable people approve conclusions and sensitive external actions.

elements.label: Objective
elements.question: What accounting outcome is being pursued?
elements.definition: State the bounded accounting outcome before selecting tools, procedures, or a desired conclusion.
elements.failure_boundary: Do not begin when the outcome, owner, or completion condition is ambiguous.

elements.label: Scope
elements.question: Which entity, period, population, framework, materiality, and exclusions apply?
elements.definition: Bind the work to the exact facts and boundaries that the accountable owner approved.
elements.failure_boundary: Stop when a source, item, period, entity, or action falls outside the recorded scope.

elements.label: Evidence
elements.question: What may support the work, and is it complete, reliable, applicable, and traceable?
elements.definition: Identify authoritative records and sources, preserve provenance, and keep contradictions and missing evidence visible.
required_record: Applicability, reliability, contradiction, and freshness notes
elements.failure_boundary: Do not infer missing facts or suppress contradictory, stale, wrong-period, or inapplicable evidence.

elements.label: Procedure
elements.question: Which model work, deterministic work, tools, and state transitions perform the task?
elements.definition: Separate probabilistic investigation and drafting from deterministic calculations, validations, and system operations.
required_record: Model, prompt, policy, and tool versions
State transitions, handoffs, and exception paths
elements.failure_boundary: Do not let model output silently replace an independently enforceable calculation, policy, or approval step.

elements.label: Checks
elements.question: Which arithmetic, tie-outs, schemas, permissions, limits, and stop conditions must pass?
elements.definition: Specify deterministic tests and hard gates before the run, including the treatment of failures and overrides.
required_record: Schema, permission, duplicate, and payload tests
Thresholds, stop conditions, and exception disposition
elements.failure_boundary: A failed hard gate cannot be averaged away by fluent output, confidence, or other passing checks.

elements.label: Authority
elements.question: What may be read, prepared, recommended, approved, executed, or represented?
elements.definition: Classify authority at the action level and enforce the smallest permission needed outside the model.
required_record: Identity, segregation of duties, and credential boundary
elements.failure_boundary: Confidence, a prompt, or the agent's own state never grants approval or execution authority.

elements.label: Review
elements.question: Who challenges the work, resolves exceptions, and owns the decision?
elements.definition: Name the competent accountable reviewer and the evidence, judgments, exceptions, and alternatives that require disposition.
required_record: Attributable approve, modify, reject, or escalate decision
elements.failure_boundary: The agent cannot approve its own work or make an accounting, fiduciary, legal, control, or professional conclusion on a person's behalf.

elements.label: Action
elements.question: How is any approved effect bound, enforced, acknowledged, and reconciled?
elements.definition: Keep preparation separate from execution and permit only the exact approved payload through a constrained interface.
required_record: Independent policy, permission, limit, and idempotency checks
Acknowledgment, reconciliation, and rollback or compensation path
elements.failure_boundary: Do not post, pay, file, delete, certify, approve, or communicate externally without separately attributable authority and deterministic enforcement.

elements.label: Record
elements.question: What workpaper, trace, versions, approvals, receipts, corrections, and retention evidence remain?
elements.definition: Retain an accounting-facing record that lets a competent reviewer reproduce the work and distinguish preparation, judgment, approval, and execution.
required_record: Procedures, checks, exceptions, versions, and approvals
Action receipt, reconciliation, correction, and retention state
elements.failure_boundary: A technical trace alone is not an accounting workpaper, and a rewritten record must not erase prior decisions or corrections.

scenarios.title: Month-end accrual and proposed journal entry
scenarios.context: Fictional Northstar Components LLC is closing September 2026. A synthetic $36,000 service contract covers August through October; service acceptance supports work through September, no invoice or accrual appears in the approved AP and ledger extracts, and the vendor has not replied.
scenarios.intended_lesson: Preparation and recommendation can be rigorous without allowing the agent to approve or post the entry.

elements.application: Prepare a supported September accrual, proposed reversal, and reviewer packet; do not approve or post.
Northstar Components LLC, September 2026, one synthetic contract, one cost center, USD, and the approved materiality and cutoff policy.
Executed synthetic contract, service acceptance, AP and ledger populations with control totals, chart of accounts, cutoff policy, and visible vendor nonresponse.

Validate populations, confirm two months of accepted service, calculate the $12,000 monthly rate and $24,000 cumulative amount through September, search for duplication, flag the unrecorded August amount for controller disposition, draft the balanced entry and reversal, and assemble exceptions.

$36,000 divided by three months equals $12,000 per month; two accepted months equal a $24,000 cumulative accrual through September; debits equal credits; entity, period, accounts, and dimensions are valid; no invoice or accrual is duplicated.
The agent prepares at A1 and may recommend at A2. The controller's accounting conclusion is human-only; any later staging action is separately approval-gated A3.

The controller challenges completeness, cutoff, the $24,000 cumulative estimate, the unrecorded August service and any prior-period implications, account classification, vendor nonresponse, and the proposed reversal before deciding.
No ledger effect occurs during preparation. After attributable approval, only the exact approved payload may enter a constrained staging queue; posting remains outside this scenario.
Retain source identifiers and totals, calculation, proposed entry and reversal, exceptions, versions, reviewer decision, payload hash if approved, and final disposition.

scenarios.accountable_conclusion: A named controller approves, modifies, rejects, or escalates the proposed treatment. The agent does not own the conclusion.

scenarios.title: Vendor payment with changed bank instructions
scenarios.context: Fictional Harbor Supply Co. has a synthetic $72,400 approved invoice and receipt match. Bank instructions printed on the invoice differ from the approved vendor master, and the requester asks for urgent release.
scenarios.intended_lesson: A payment can proceed only after independent verification, conflict resolution, payload-bound approval, and deterministic bank controls.

elements.application: Prepare a payment decision package and release only a separately verified, approved payload; otherwise hold and escalate.
One fictional vendor, invoice, legal entity, bank account, currency, value date, payment rail, and approved payment limit.
Invoice, purchase order, receipt, vendor master, change request, independent callback record, sanctions result, requester identity, and cash availability.
Reperform the match, isolate the conflicting bank data, verify the beneficiary through an independent channel, screen applicable controls, identify role conflicts, and prepare the immutable payload.
Invoice, receipt, and PO agree; beneficiary is independently verified; sanctions and fraud holds are clear; approvers are authorized; payload hash and duplicate key pass.
The agent may prepare and recommend. Vendor-master approval and fiduciary payment approval are human-owned. A constrained tool may transmit one exact approved payload at A3.
Authorized vendor-master and treasury reviewers resolve the changed instructions, urgency, segregation-of-duties conflict, and any screening exception.
Hold on unresolved verification or conflict. If all gates pass, transmit the exact approved payload once, preserve bank acknowledgment, and reconcile settlement.
Retain all source records, independent verification, screening evidence, role checks, approvals, payload hash, idempotency key, acknowledgment, settlement reconciliation, and any incident record.

scenarios.accountable_conclusion: Authorized people approve the beneficiary and payment. The agent cannot infer approval from urgency, an invoice, a message, or its own confidence.

workflow_mapping.boundary: Every workflow exposes the same nine element IDs and points each element to canonical workflow fields. Mapping does not grant authority or professional review.

summary: Classify an accounting action by its effect, distinguish preparation from execution, and identify the accountable approval boundary.

provenance.note: Migrated from the existing project corpus. Import and integrity checks are not source verification or professional review.

data.review_note: Maintainer review is pending. Subject-matter, independent, professional, audit, or assurance review is not claimed.
data.intended_audience: Accounting practitioners, reviewers, control owners, transformation leaders, and builders who need to classify one proposed agent action.
prerequisites: Name one observable action and the system or record it may affect.
Identify the accountable owner and any required approver before assigning an authority level.
data.expected_outcome: Assign the smallest proposed action to A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, or human-only; identify the controls and separation of duties required; and stop when the action cannot be bounded safely.

operating_rule.text: Agents may prepare accounting work. Accountable people approve conclusions and sensitive external actions.

decision_steps.question: Can you state one observable action, its target, and its possible effect?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: Authority belongs to actions, not to a product name, model, workflow, or confidence score.

yes.label: Test whether the responsibility is inherently human-owned.

no.label: Stop and split the workflow into smaller actions.

decision_steps.question: Does the action approve an accounting conclusion, sign or certify, exercise fiduciary discretion, or assume a person's identity?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: These responsibilities remain attributable to an authorized person even when an agent prepares the support.

yes.label: Human-only. The agent may prepare support but may not perform the act.

no.label: Determine whether the action is informational.

decision_steps.question: Does the action only explain or retrieve approved information without changing a work record?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: A response that creates no work record or external effect is educational or informational, not approval.

no.label: Determine whether the action only prepares work.

decision_steps.question: Does the action collect, normalize, calculate, classify, or draft evidence-linked work without choosing the conclusion?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: Preparation may be substantial while still leaving judgment and approval with named people.

no.label: Determine whether the action recommends a judgment.

decision_steps.question: Does the action propose a conclusion or treatment while a named person accepts, modifies, rejects, or escalates it?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: A recommendation may frame judgment but cannot inherit the accountable person's decision authority.

decision_steps.question: Is this one exact action or payload already approved by an attributable person and independently verifiable by the executing tool?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: A3 is a narrow commit step after approval, not general permission to decide, edit, or expand the payload.

yes.label: A3 — Execute the exact approved action once, within enforced limits.

no.label: Test whether a low-risk policy can authorize the action.

decision_steps.question: Is the effect low-risk, reversible, non-fiduciary, and allowed by deterministic policy with monitoring and exception routing?
decision_steps.why_it_matters: A4 relies on policy and reversibility; model confidence or prior success is not the policy engine.

no.label: Stop. Route the action to an authorized person or redesign it as preparation.

stop_conditions: The action, target, entity, period, amount, recipient, or possible effect is not specific.
Required evidence is missing, contradictory, stale, or outside the approved scope.
The proposed authority depends on model confidence, fluency, prior success, a chat response, or silence.
Approval is not attributable, current, within the person's authority, and bound to the exact payload.
The executing tool cannot independently enforce identity, scope, limits, payload integrity, and idempotency.
One actor can prepare, alter the payload, approve, execute, and conceal or reconcile the same action without independent challenge.
The action is a final conclusion, signature, attestation, certification, fiduciary decision, or other inherently human-owned responsibility.

execution_comparison.entry_condition: A named person has approved the exact action or immutable payload.
execution_comparison.decision_owner: The person owns the conclusion and approval; deterministic controls authorize only the matching execution call.
execution_comparison.permitted_effect: One constrained, idempotent action within approved entity, period, accounts, amount, recipient, and time limits.
execution_comparison.accounting_example: Submit an approved journal-entry payload to an ERP staging queue without changing its lines or posting beyond the approved interface.
execution_comparison.stop_when: The payload, authority, limit, system state, or approval changes or cannot be verified.

execution_comparison.entry_condition: A deterministic policy permits a low-risk, reversible, non-accounting effect without a new case-specific approval.
execution_comparison.decision_owner: The policy owner defines the rule; the policy engine, not the model, allows or rejects the action.
execution_comparison.permitted_effect: Only the reversible operational effect named by policy, with monitoring and exception routing.
execution_comparison.accounting_example: Mark a close task complete when required evidence fields and deterministic dependency checks pass, without posting or locking the period.
execution_comparison.stop_when: The effect becomes material, irreversible, externally attributable, fiduciary, or dependent on judgment.

execution_comparison.entry_condition: The act carries accounting, legal, fiduciary, control, professional, or external accountability.
execution_comparison.decision_owner: An identified and authorized person directly reviews the current evidence and performs the act.
execution_comparison.permitted_effect: The agent may prepare a decision packet; it may not click, sign, attest, certify, approve, or impersonate the person.
execution_comparison.accounting_example: Approve the accounting treatment, release a material payment, sign an ICFR certification, or authorize final close.
execution_comparison.stop_when: Always stop the agent before the human-owned act; preserve the attributable decision separately.

mixed_level_workflow.title: Synthetic accrual entry and close-task walkthrough
mixed_level_workflow.context: A fictional entity is preparing an August 2026 expense accrual. The evidence, proposed entry, approval, staging submission, close-task status, and reporting certification are separate actions.

actions.action: Retrieve and explain the approved accrual policy.
actions.why: No work record or accounting effect is created.
actions.accountable_person: Policy owner maintains the approved guidance.

actions.action: Assemble evidence, calculate the estimate, and draft balanced entry lines.
actions.why: The agent prepares evidence-linked work but does not choose or approve the conclusion.
actions.accountable_person: Preparer and reviewer challenge completeness and calculation.

actions.action: Recommend the accrual treatment and show alternatives, uncertainty, and proposed reversal.
actions.why: A recommendation frames judgment while the named reviewer decides.
actions.accountable_person: Authorized reviewer accepts, modifies, rejects, or escalates.

actions.action: Approve the accounting conclusion and exact entry payload.
actions.why: Approval assigns accounting accountability and cannot be inferred from agent confidence.
actions.accountable_person: Authorized approver performs an attributable decision.

actions.action: Submit the unchanged approved payload once to the ERP staging queue.
actions.why: Execution follows approval of the exact payload and is independently constrained.
actions.accountable_person: Approver owns the decision; system owner owns the constrained interface.

actions.action: Mark the close task complete when specified evidence and dependency checks pass.
actions.why: The status change is reversible, non-accounting, and permitted only by deterministic policy.
actions.accountable_person: Close owner defines and monitors the policy.

actions.action: Authorize final close or certify the reporting result.
actions.why: Final close and certification carry control, legal, and external accountability.

mixed_level_workflow.finished_artifact: An action register that records each stable action ID, authority level, responsible person, required approval, enforcement point, stop condition, and retained evidence.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: High model confidence turns a recommendation into an approval.
common_misclassifications.correction: Confidence may inform review but never changes A2 into human approval authority.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: The entire agent or workflow is A3.
common_misclassifications.correction: Classify each action. One workflow may contain A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, and human-only steps.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: A person saying “looks good” in chat is enough for A3.
common_misclassifications.correction: Approval must be authenticated, attributable, within authority, current, and bound to the exact payload.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: Any reversible action qualifies for A4.
common_misclassifications.correction: A4 also requires low risk, deterministic policy, monitoring, exception routing, and no human-owned judgment.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: Submitting to a staging queue is always harmless preparation.
common_misclassifications.correction: Classify the actual effect and permissions. A staging write is A3 when it changes a controlled system after exact approval.

common_misclassifications.mistaken_claim: Any human in the loop provides segregation of duties.
common_misclassifications.correction: The person must be identified, authorized, appropriately independent, and unable to approve a payload they or the agent can silently change afterward.

segregation_of_duties_examples.unsafe_combination: The same agent prepares an entry and treats its own recommendation as approval.
segregation_of_duties_examples.safer_design: The agent prepares under A1/A2; an authorized person approves the exact payload; a constrained tool performs any A3 submission.
segregation_of_duties_examples.principle: Preparation, approval, and execution remain distinguishable and attributable.

segregation_of_duties_examples.unsafe_combination: One identity changes vendor bank data and releases the resulting payment.
segregation_of_duties_examples.safer_design: Independent verification and approval govern master-data change; payment preparation and release use separate roles and credentials.
segregation_of_duties_examples.principle: Maintenance, payment preparation, and fiduciary release are incompatible duties.

segregation_of_duties_examples.unsafe_combination: The executor can edit an approved payload before sending it.
segregation_of_duties_examples.safer_design: Approval binds an immutable payload hash; the executing tool rejects any field or version difference.
segregation_of_duties_examples.principle: Approval applies to the exact effect, not a general request.

segregation_of_duties_examples.unsafe_combination: The executor is the only party that checks and clears its own result.
segregation_of_duties_examples.safer_design: Preserve the execution receipt and reconcile it independently to the approved payload and authoritative system.
segregation_of_duties_examples.principle: Execution evidence is challenged separately from execution.

sensitive_action_mappings.rule: Prepare and recommend under A1/A2; keep conclusion approval human-owned; use A3 only for the exact approved payload.
The agent may prepare a payment packet; fiduciary approval remains human-owned; any A3 submission must be exact, one-time, and independently authorized.
Always human-only when the decision carries accounting, legal, fiduciary, control, professional, or external accountability.
The agent may prepare support but may not sign, click, attest, certify, or assume the certifier's identity.
A4 may update a reversible task status under deterministic policy; final close, period lock, material override, and reporting certification remain human-owned.

limitations: The A0–A4 labels and decision tree are an Accounting Agents implementation pattern, not a professional standard or grant of authority.
The correct classification depends on the exact action, system effect, entity, period, amount, evidence, jurisdiction, policy, and accountable roles.
A lower-risk label does not replace current legal, regulatory, contractual, accounting, audit, security, or organizational requirements.
Maintainer review and automated tests are not subject-matter review, independent assurance, certification, or professional sign-off.
data.next_action: Choose one real or synthetic workflow, split it into observable actions, apply the decision tree to each action, and carry the resulting action register into the Control Model and sensitive-action guidance.

source_basis.scope: COSO internal-control principles support accountability, control activities, information, and monitoring; applicability depends on the entity's adopted framework and facts.
The 2025 Green Book addresses authority, responsibility, segregation of duties, access, and control activities for US federal entities; outside that scope it is guidance, not binding law.
PCAOB AS 2201 informs ICFR responsibility and control evaluation in in-scope public-company audits; it does not adopt the A0–A4 labels.

NIST SP 800-53 provides control patterns for access enforcement, least privilege, separation of duties, audit records, and change control; applicability depends on the system and adopted control baseline.

title: Authority decision guide
Agent fundamentals
summary: An accounting agent pursues a defined accounting objective. It can select steps, use approved tools and evidence, inspect results, and continue until it reaches a completion or stop condition.

provenance.note: Migrated from the existing project corpus. Import and integrity checks are not source verification or professional review.

data.title: Agent fundamentals
data.summary: An accounting agent pursues a defined accounting objective. It can select steps, use approved tools and evidence, inspect results, and continue until it reaches a completion or stop condition.
paragraphs: Definition
An accounting agent pursues a defined accounting objective. It can select steps, use approved tools and evidence, inspect results, and continue until it reaches a completion or stop condition.
A usable definition names four things: the objective, available tools, accepted evidence, and operating limits. A product label alone does not describe the system's authority.

See OpenAI's practical guide to building agents.
Objective
The accounting outcome, entity, period, and scope.
Tools
The data and actions the system can access.
Evidence
The sources accepted for facts and calculations.
Limits
The thresholds, approvals, prohibitions, and stop conditions.
Four operating patterns

Classify a system by who or what controls the next step. This avoids relying on product language that uses agent for several different behaviors.Comparison of chat, copilot, workflow, and agent operating patterns
| Pattern | Next step controlled by | Behavior | Accounting example
| Chat | Person | Answers a prompt | Explain a lease-accounting concept.
| Copilot | Person | Assists inside a task | Draft a variance explanation for review.
| Workflow | Defined rules | Runs a fixed sequence | Match invoices when specified fields agree.
| Agent | Model within set limits | Selects steps and tools | Investigate unmatched cash items and route exceptions.
Work loop

An agent run should leave a path that a reviewer can follow. Use the following sequence as a baseline, then adapt it to the workflow.
1
Objective

Define the outcome, period, scope, and stop conditions.
2
Evidence

Collect source records and record where each fact came from.
3
Plan

Break the objective into work units and identify required approvals.
4
Work

Use approved tools to normalize, compare, calculate, research, and draft.
5
Check

Run tie-outs, thresholds, completeness tests, and other deterministic checks.
6
Review
Send exceptions, judgments, and proposed effects to the accountable reviewer.
Run record

Store more than the final answer. Record the objective, source set, procedures, tool calls, calculations, exceptions, contradictory evidence, configuration, approvals, and conclusion. The record should show who prepared and reviewed the work and when each action occurred.
Trace and workpaper serve different jobs
A technical trace helps diagnose the system. A governed workpaper explains the accounting work to its intended reviewer. Convert the relevant trace data into the required workpaper format.
See PCAOB AS 1215, Audit Documentation.

data.title: System architecture for accounting agents
data.summary: Prompts become difficult to review when they contain the accounting method, access rules, approval policy, output format, and quality tests in one block. Store each concern where the system can version, test, and approve it.System layers, purposes, and account
paragraphs: Separate the system layers

Prompts become difficult to review when they contain the accounting method, access rules, approval policy, output format, and quality tests in one block. Store each concern where the system can version, test, and approve it.System layers, purposes, and accounting-agent examples
| Layer | Purpose | Example
| Skill | Method for performing the accounting work | Reconcile cash
| Tool | Interface the system can read or use | Read a ledger export
| Policy | Rule that limits the system's authority | Draft only; do not post
| Template | Required structure for the output | Reconciliation workpaper
| Evaluator | Test applied to the result | Balance ties; evidence linked
Keep the accounting record outside the model

The agent runtime executes model and tool calls. The accounting application owns work state, evidence, policies, approvals, and history. A model or provider change should not break the work record.
Work item
Objective, entity, period, owner, scope, and status.
Work plan
Versioned procedures, assigned work units, and approval points.
Run
Instructions, model, tools, configuration, inputs, and timestamps.
Evidence item
Source, provenance, version, period, and access record.
Finding
Observation, support, contradiction, severity, and disposition.
Proposed effect
Draft entry, adjustment, disclosure, task, or escalation.
Review
Reviewer decision, comments, date, and required rework.
Commit boundary
The approval required before an external action becomes effective.
Carry work forward by reference
Keep completed work in history. Require an explicit decision before a later period or run treats that work as current evidence.
Use the simplest orchestration that works

Begin with one general accounting agent and deterministic helpers. Add specialist agents when a single instruction set becomes difficult to evaluate or when separate context improves the result.
Use code-controlled steps when sequence and outcome must remain predictable.
Use model-controlled steps for investigation, classification, and evidence requests.
Use deterministic code for calculations, tie-outs, schema checks, and permissions.
Pause the run before sensitive tools or material judgments.
Return specialist results to one accountable manager for the final package.
Treat tool protocols as interfaces

Model Context Protocol can expose ledger data, policies, evidence stores, calculations, and actions through narrow interfaces. The protocol does not establish data completeness, authorization, segregation of duties, or ICFR readiness.
Validate inputs and outputs, separate read and write tools, enforce permissions outside the model, require approval for sensitive actions, and log the request and result.
See the OpenAI Agents SDK documentation and Model Context Protocol specification.

data.title: Evidence and assurance
data.summary:
Separate what a source says from what the system infers and what an accountable person decides. A linked chain makes disagreement, missing support, and judgment visible before a conclusion is used.
01Evidence
paragraphs: Keep the reasoning chain visible

Separate what a source says from what the system infers and what an accountable person decides. A linked chain makes disagreement, missing support, and judgment visible before a conclusion is used.
01Evidence

An invoice states $24,000 and covers June through August.
02Observation

One month of service relates to the current reporting period.
03Claim

The supported current-period expense is $8,000.
04Judgment

The amount exceeds the team's review threshold.
05Decision
The reviewer approves the proposed entry.
Contradictory evidence is part of the record
Do not average it away, omit it from a summary, or treat confidence as resolution. Link the conflict to the affected claim and route it to the named reviewer.
Evaluate evidence before using itEvidence-reliability dimensions, review questions, and retained support
| Dimension | Question | Retained evidence
| Authenticity | Who produced or controls the source, and has custody been preserved? | System, owner, identifier, hash, or retrieval record
| Completeness | Does the population include every in-scope record exactly once? | Extraction parameters, counts, amounts, exclusions, and tie-out
| Accuracy | Do fields and calculations agree with authoritative records? | Independent recalculation, validation, and exception results
| Relevance | Does the evidence support the specific assertion or decision? | Claim-to-source mapping and procedure
| Applicability | Does the rule or evidence apply to this entity, period, transaction, and jurisdiction? | Scope analysis and effective version
| Timeliness | Was the source current at the time of the work and decision? | As-of date, retrieval time, and subsequent-event check
| Consistency | What corroborates or contradicts the source? | Alternative sources, differences, and reviewer disposition
Build an accounting workpaper, not only a trace

Technical traces help diagnose orchestration and tool behavior. The workpaper must also let a competent reviewer understand the accounting objective, evidence, procedure, result, exceptions, and proposed effect.
Identify entity, period, population, jurisdiction, materiality, and accountable roles.
Preserve source owners, versions, extraction parameters, control totals, and transformations.
Link each material observation and claim to its evidence and reproducible calculation.
Show contrary evidence, uncertainty, stop events, overrides, and unresolved questions prominently.
Record model, prompt, policy, tool, template, and evaluator versions used for the run.
Retain reviewer decisions, exact approval payloads, execution receipts, and corrections.

Separate support, performance, and assessment
Preparation
The agent organizes evidence, reproduces calculations, drafts work, and identifies exceptions.
Performance
The designated control performer executes the defined procedure at the required precision and frequency.
Review
A competent person challenges the work, resolves exceptions, and makes the assigned decision.
Assessment
Management, internal audit, or an external auditor evaluates design or effectiveness under the applicable framework.
Representation
An authorized person makes any final attestation, certification, audit conclusion, or external statement.
No self-assurance
The agent's explanation of its own work is not independent evidence that the work is correct or that a control operated effectively.
Control patterns for evidence
Input completeness and control totals

Establish the authoritative source, extraction parameters, and independent population totals before work begins.
Risk
The agent works from a partial, duplicated, stale, or wrong-scope population.
Owner
Workflow owner
Frequency
Every run

Procedure
Record source system, entity, period, query, and timestamp
Reproduce counts and amounts
Reconcile transformations and exclusions
Stop on unexplained difference

Evidence
Source register
Raw and transformed control totals
Exclusion and transformation log
Source authenticity and applicability

Use identifiable, current, applicable evidence and preserve its provenance.
Risk
Evidence is altered, unauthoritative, inapplicable, or from the wrong entity, period, or jurisdiction.
Owner
Preparer and reviewer
Frequency
Every source and run

Procedure
Identify source owner and custody
Verify version and effective date
Confirm entity, period, jurisdiction, and claim linkage
Retain contradictory evidence

Evidence
Source URL or system identifier
Version and retrieval date
Applicability rationale
Deterministic recalculation and tie-outs

Use deterministic code and source totals for arithmetic, validation, permissions, and completion criteria.
Risk
A plausible narrative hides a calculation, schema, completeness, or balancing error.
Owner
Workflow owner
Frequency
Every run and before action

Procedure
Recalculate independently
Validate schemas and allowed values
Tie inputs, outputs, and proposed effects
Block action when a hard check fails

Evidence
Validation result
Independent calculation
Tie-out and error log
Configuration, version, and run evidence

Preserve the exact configuration, sources, actions, results, and actors for each run.
Risk
The work cannot be reproduced or attributed after a model, source, tool, or policy changes.
Owner
System and workflow owners
Frequency
Every run

Procedure
Record model, prompt, policy, tool, template, evaluator, and source versions
Capture tool calls and results
Link approvals and final disposition

Evidence
Technical trace
Accounting run record
Workpaper and approval history
Control performance and assessment separation

Keep preparation and performance evidence separate from management's or the auditor's final assessment.
Risk
The system that performs or prepares a control also concludes that the control operated effectively.
Owner
Management evaluator, internal audit, or external auditor as applicable
Frequency
Every control assessment

Procedure
Identify preparer, performer, owner, tester, and assessor
Preserve exceptions and limitations
Require independent human evaluation where the framework demands it

Evidence
Role assignment
Control workpaper
Independent assessment and sign-off

paragraphs: Give the system its own attributable identity

An accounting agent should act as a non-human workload with an identifiable owner, workflow, environment, and permission set. It should not borrow a person's session, API key, mailbox, signer credential, or approval authority.
Workload identity
Identifies the deployed service, agent, and environment for every request.
Human identity
Identifies the requester, reviewer, approver, or operator and their current authority.
Workflow identity
Binds activity to an approved objective, version, entity, period, and run.
Tool identity
Identifies the constrained interface and records the policy decision for each call.
A model is not a principal
The surrounding system authenticates the workload, assigns scope, evaluates policy, and records the actor. Never treat fluent text as proof of identity, permission, or approval.

Authorize every tool call
Authenticate.Verify workload and human identities using current, non-shared credentials.
Bind context.Attach workflow, run, entity, period, purpose, data classification, and requested action.
Evaluate policy.Check allowed tool, fields, records, amount, time, authority level, and segregation conflicts.
Verify approval.For A3, authenticate the approver and match the exact, unexpired payload.
Execute narrowly.Use field-level permissions, idempotency, transaction limits, and deny-by-default behavior.
Record and reconcile.Log the decision and result, compare it with the approved intent, and route differences.
The prompt is not the policy engine
A prompt may explain the rule to the model. Only deterministic authorization can reliably enforce identity, scope, amount, approval state, payload integrity, and prohibited actions.
Preserve segregation of duties

Agents can collapse roles accidentally when a single tool bundle can request, maintain master data, approve, execute, reconcile, and delete evidence. Map incompatible responsibilities at the action level and enforce them across human and non-human identities.Segregation-of-duties conflicts and enforcement examples
| Responsibility | Conflict to prevent | Example enforcement
| Request | Requesting and approving the same action | Independent approver role and policy decision
| Master data | Changing beneficiary data and releasing payment | Separate tools, identities, and verification evidence
| Preparation | Preparing and finally approving accounting work | Named reviewer with no model-delegated approval
| Execution | Executing and concealing an unauthorized effect | Immutable logs and independent reconciliation
| Assessment | Performing a control and assessing its own effectiveness | Independent human evaluator and retained exceptions

Limit data, secrets, and persistence
Classify data before use and restrict collection to the approved accounting purpose.
Prefer scoped connectors or short-lived tokens over copied credentials and broad exports.
Minimize fields, redact unnecessary personal data, and isolate entities and environments.
Define provider use, location, retention, training, subprocessors, export, and deletion terms.
Keep secrets out of prompts, traces, workpapers, evaluation sets, and reviewer packets.
Honor accounting-record retention, privacy obligations, investigations, and legal holds together.
Test revocation, tool denial, provider outage, compromise, data export, and exit procedures.

Procedure

Deny by default
Review denials and entitlements

Wildcard permission
Write access without approval enforcement

Require a named authorized person to approve the exact decision or payload before sensitive action.
Risk
The agent infers, fabricates, reuses, or expands approval.

Accountable process owner

Procedure
Present evidence, exceptions, and exact payload
Authenticate approver and authority
Record approval conditions and expiration
Reject payload drift

Segregation of duties

Separate incompatible responsibilities and prevent the agent from collapsing them through shared credentials or tools.
Risk
One person or agent can initiate, alter master data, approve, execute, and conceal a transaction.
Owner
Process and security owners

At design, access change, and periodic review

Block incompatible combinations

Understand the service boundary, data use, controls, dependencies, change process, and exit plan.
Risk
A provider's model, service, subprocessor, availability, or terms create unassessed accounting, security, or continuity risk.

Data classification, privacy, and retention

Limit data to the approved purpose, access, location, retention period, and disposal method.
Risk
Sensitive, personal, privileged, or regulated data is exposed, retained, reused, or destroyed improperly.

Data, privacy, legal, and system owners

At design, every new data source, and periodic review

Unknown training or reuse

Incident containment, rollback, and evidence preservation

Stop impact, preserve evidence, determine scope, correct records, and learn before resuming.
Risk
An erroneous or unauthorized action continues, evidence is lost, or affected accounting records remain uncorrected.
Owner
Incident commander with accounting, security, legal, and system owners
Frequency
On incident with periodic exercises

Procedure

Preserve runs, approvals, and system evidence
Identify affected populations and outputs
Reverse or compensate through authorized procedures

data.title: Production operations
data.summary:
Production begins when real users, records, decisions, or actions can depend on the workflow. Before that point, assign owners, freeze the approved version, test failure paths, and prove that the team can deny, pause, recover, and reconcile the system.

paragraphs: Do not operate what the team cannot stop

Production begins when real users, records, decisions, or actions can depend on the workflow. Before that point, assign owners, freeze the approved version, test failure paths, and prove that the team can deny, pause, recover, and reconcile the system.
Accounting, system, control, security, vendor, and incident owners are named.
The approved workflow, authority matrix, tools, data, limits, and evaluation results are versioned.
Write paths are least-privilege, approval-bound, idempotent, observable, and independently reconciled.
Alerts have thresholds, an on-call owner, response time, escalation path, and pause action.
Run records, workpapers, approvals, receipts, and source versions meet retention requirements.
Fallback, provider outage, credential revocation, rollback, correction, and exit procedures have been exercised.
Monitor accounting outcomes and system behaviorProduction monitoring signals and required responses
| Signal family | Examples | Response
| Population | Untied totals, exclusions, duplicates, incomplete runs | Stop the run; re-establish source completeness
| Quality | Calculation error, unsupported claim, missed exception, rising reviewer rework | Limit scope; review affected outputs; add regression cases
| Authority | Tool denial, approval bypass, payload drift, self-approval, duplicate action | Pause write path immediately; preserve authorization evidence
| Accounting | Unreconciled effect, post-close adjustment, corrected filing, stale open item | Identify affected records; correct through authorized procedures
| Operations | Latency, timeout, retry loop, cost spike, unavailable provider, failed receipt | Degrade safely, fail closed, and invoke continuity plan
| Change | New model, prompt, policy, source, tool, schema, vendor, or jurisdiction | Reassess and rerun the applicable evaluation gate
Pause on control failure

If scope, approval, permission, completeness, payload integrity, or reconciliation cannot be established, fail closed and preserve the current state. Do not ask the model to reason around a failed control.

Treat behavior changes as production changes
Identify.Record the changed model, prompt, tool, source, policy, template, evaluator, infrastructure, or dependency.
Assess.Map affected workflows, assertions, actions, data, jurisdictions, controls, and retained work.
Evaluate.Run applicable regression, edge, adversarial, tool, authorization, and recovery cases.
Approve.Record the accountable release decision, conditions, residual risk, timing, and rollback version.
Observe.Use heightened monitoring after release and compare quality, overrides, exceptions, and system behavior.
Use the production change record to preserve the decision and the evaluation plan to define the evidence needed for release.

Contain, preserve, determine, correct
ContainDisable affected tools, revoke credentials, pause workflows, and stop downstream use.
PreserveRetain runs, prompts, versions, sources, approvals, tool results, system logs, and affected outputs.
DetermineEstablish timeline, root cause, entities, periods, populations, records, users, and external parties affected.
CorrectReverse or compensate through authorized accounting procedures and reconcile every affected effect.
CommunicateUse legal, privacy, security, audit, governance, customer, or regulator processes as applicable.
LearnAdd regression cases, redesign the control, reassess risk, and require approval before resuming.
Record the event with the incident report. Never silently edit or delete the original run, approval, or accounting record.

Run a recurring operating review
Scope
Active workflows, versions, populations, authority levels, users, tools, vendors, and jurisdictions.
Quality
Coverage, accuracy, exceptions, rework, overrides, disagreement, and downstream corrections.
Controls
Denied actions, approval integrity, segregation conflicts, access reviews, control failures, and remediation.
Change
Released and pending changes, evaluation results, drift, provider notices, and new requirements.
Incidents
Events, near misses, affected records, time to contain, correction, root cause, and open actions.
Decision
Continue, constrain, pause, correct, retrain, redesign, replace, or retire with an accountable owner.
Related controls
Model, prompt, policy, and configuration change
Release only identified, tested, approved versions with a rollback path.

Procedure
Record changed artifact and reason
Run regression and workflow evaluations
Approve release against risk criteria
Monitor and retain prior version

Evaluation results
Approval and deployment record
Override and reviewer-disagreement monitoring
Measure overrides, disagreements, exceptions, and downstream corrections by version and workflow.

Procedure

Trend by model, prompt, tool, source, and workflow
Set escalation thresholds
Feed resolved cases into evaluation

Evidence

Trend report
Remediation and evaluation result
Configuration, version, and run evidence
Preserve the exact configuration, sources, actions, results, and actors for each run.

Procedure

Capture tool calls and results
Link approvals and final disposition

Production monitoring and kill switch
Detect material change, policy breach, failure, and drift early enough to contain impact.

Procedure
Monitor quality, exceptions, overrides, latency, tool errors, and denied actions
Set alert and pause thresholds

paragraphs: Start with the release decision

An evaluation should answer a concrete question: whether a defined workflow version may enter shadow use, prepare drafts, reach a limited population, receive a constrained tool, or continue after a change. Measure the end-to-end accounting outcome, not only model response quality.
Unit under test
Workflow, model, instructions, sources, tools, policy, template, evaluator, and environment as one versioned system.
Decision owner
Named accounting process owner with system, risk, control, security, legal, or audit input as applicable.
Risk basis
Materiality, reversibility, external effect, assertion, data sensitivity, frequency, and ability to detect and recover.
Expected result
Independently derived answer, evidence, check, stop, or reviewer decision with provenance.
Build cases from the workflow and its failures
Normal
Representative in-policy populations, formats, systems, entities, and periods with known results.
Edge
Boundary dates, rounding, currencies, reversals, duplicates, sparse support, large populations, and threshold values.
Contradictory
Sources disagree, facts change, guidance conflicts, or support does not match the requested accounting effect.
Unauthorized
Wrong entity, period, user, tool, field, amount, account, recipient, payload, or expired approval.
Adversarial
Prompt injection, malicious documents, data exfiltration attempts, forged approval, or tool-result manipulation.
Failure and recovery
Tool timeout, duplicate request, partial write, stale source, outage, policy denial, rollback, and rerun.

paragraphs: Before the pilot

Assign a business owner, technical owner, control owner, and reviewer. Document the current process and collect a small set of representative, edge, contradictory, and known-answer cases.
The workflow has a defined objective and reviewer.
Source access is authorized and limited to the required data.
The team can reproduce control totals and key calculations.
The expected output and review standard are documented.
The system can stop without changing a record or sending a message.
The team can restore the prior configuration after a change.

Pilot stages
1
Choose the scope

Select one repeatable workflow with stable evidence and a named reviewer.
2
Write the specification

Define inputs, output, checks, authority limits, and stop conditions.
3
Run in shadow mode

Use read-only access beside the current process. Do not change records.
4
Prepare drafts

Let the agent prepare work. Require approval for judgments and external actions.
5
Measure the result

Track coverage, accuracy, exceptions, rework, cycle time, and reviewer overrides.
6
Set the next boundary
Expand only when the run record supports a wider scope or authority.
MeasuresMeasures for evaluating a supervised accounting-agent pilot
| Measure | Question
| Coverage | How much of the defined population did the run process?
| Accuracy | Did calculations, matches, classifications, and citations agree with known answers?
| Exception quality | Did the run find material problems without creating excessive false positives?
| Traceability | Can the reviewer follow each material result to its source and procedure?
| Rework | How much preparation and correction did the reviewer perform?
| Cycle time | How long did preparation, review, correction, and approval take?
| Overrides | Which agent recommendations did reviewers reject or change, and why?
Stop conditions

Pause the pilot and investigate when any of these conditions occur:
The source population cannot be tied to an authoritative control total.
The agent uses an unauthorized source or tool.
A material result lacks support or contradicts source evidence.
The system performs or attempts a prohibited action.
Reviewer overrides increase after a model, prompt, tool, or mapping change.
The run record cannot reproduce the result or identify the configuration used.
Expansion decision
Record the evidence that supports any wider scope, tool access, or action authority. Keep the current boundary when results remain mixed or the review burden offsets the time saved.
